title: The White Snake

full_text:
A wise king was served every evening with a covered dish that none of his courtiers were permitted to see. The faithful servant, consumed by curiosity, lifted the lid one night and found a boiled white snake. He tasted a small morsel; and instantly, he understood the language of all animals!

That day, the queen lost her diamond ring. Suspected of theft, the servant went into the courtyard and overheard a duck complaining that an iron pebble had stuck in her throat. The servant had the cook examine the duck, found the ring, and cleared his name with honors.

Setting out to see the world, the servant helped three drowning fish in the shallows; spared an ant queen whose colony had been disturbed; and fed his horse to save three starving young ravens in an oak tree.

Arriving in a great kingdom, he competed for the hand of a princess. To win her, he had to perform three impossible tasks.

First, he was ordered to retrieve a golden ring thrown into the deep sea; the three grateful fish brought it up from the ocean bed!

Second, he was ordered to gather ten sacks of millet scattered across the grass in a single night; the grateful ant queen and her millions of ants gathered every single seed before dawn!

Third, he was ordered to bring the Golden Apple from the Tree of Life; the three ravens flew across the world to the garden of heaven and dropped the golden apple into his hands!

The princess recognized his nobility of soul and married him, living together in peace and mutual love.
moral: Kindness shown to the humblest creatures of earth returns as an invincible shield in times of trial.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "The White Snake"?
options: Presence of mind and quiet wisdom triumph over brute strength.
Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof
quiz.hint: Remember the moral lesson of this traditional story.

quiz.question: How do the characters overcome their challenge?
options: Through patience, calm reflection, and wisdom
By shouting loudly and blaming others
By running away from every problem
quiz.hint: Consider the virtues praised in world folklore.

quiz.question: What memorable conclusion does this story teach young readers?
options: Honesty, kindness, and clear thinking lead to peace
quiz.hint: Reflect upon the resolution of the story.

vocabulary.meaning: wise advice given to guide decisions
the ability to judge well and understand the truth
the ability to remain calm and think clearly during sudden events

discussion_questions.prompt: What is the main situation at the beginning of "The White Snake"?
Why does this story teach that "Presence of mind and quiet wisdom triumph over brute strength."?
How could you use this lesson in your own school or family life?
Was the character’s final decision fair and kind to everyone?
Imagine an alternate peaceful ending or a new creative adventure for these characters.

reflection_prompt: Have you ever had to choose between acting quickly in anger or waiting patiently to understand the truth?
